newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Additional strings on Telekom no good, BT says.
newsitem.headline: Additional strings on Telekom no good, BT says.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Thursday that the European Commission would have been better to delay Deutsche Telekom's price discounts rather than put additional conditions on the controversial plan.

"We welcome the additional conditions the Commission is apparently going to attach, but we are extremely concerned about the issue of timing," Larry Stone, BT's head of European Union affairs, told Reuters.
"This is because if Deustche Telekom is allowed to go ahead with the tariffs it will tie in customers before its competitors have the chance to compete for them," Stone said.
"(It would have been better) not to allow this tariff to proceed at all until such time as the conditions are up and running," he added.

EU sources said on Thursday that the Commission would be attaching new conditions to the tariffs, regarding the right for new telecoms companies to interconnect with Telekom's infrastructure and the issue of "break-in, break-out access" in particular to business networks.

The conditions, which would require regulatory changes in Germany, would have to be met before the end of the year with retroactive effect to November 1 when Deutsche Telekom's discount policy comes into force.
But BT's Stone said this was not enough to ensure fair competition.

The reality was that rival companies still did not know how much they would pay in the future to use Deutsche Telekom's infrastructure, he said. It also took several months to lease lines from the German telecoms giant and to connect with its network.
